messages:
ajay.p: Heads-up — after rolling a svc config change for models/llm-infer in us-west1, clients saw 503s for about ~2m. Pods are Ready, but kube-proxy logs show SYN retransmits and some IPs not matching endpoints. Anyone seen EndpointSlice weirdness like this?

devon.c: Can you paste `kubectl get endpointslice -n models -l kubernetes.io/service-name=llm-infer -o yaml`? Did the svc type or ports change during the rollout?

ajay.p: Paste of the two slices (trimmed):
```
# endpointslice-1
endpoints:
  - addresses: [10.24.5.12]
ports:
  - name: http
    port: 8080
# endpointslice-2 (stale)
endpoints:
  - addresses: [10.24.5.12, 10.24.5.13]
ports:
  - name: http
    port: 8081  # old port
```
Looks like one slice still advertising the old port 8081. Service was updated from 8081->8080 during the deploy.

lucy.k: That rings a bell — we saw duplicated/overlapping EndpointSlices when the endpointslice-controller was lagging during mass pod churn. Controller can temporarily leave stale slices with previous port metadata. Kube-proxy can sync iptables/ipvs to those stale entries and cause traffic to go to wrong NAT entries.

keegan: Also remember we have an NLB in front with nodePort egress. If kube-proxy kept NodePort entries pointing to old ports, the NLB health checks could have marked nodes healthy incorrectly or blackholed traffic.

sre-bot: incidentbot: svc update v2 rolled at 1799000050 by @ajay.p — endpointslice-controller reconciliation started.

devon.c: Quick remediation that worked in past: restart kube-proxy on affected nodes so it rebuilds iptables/ipvs, and delete the stale EndpointSlice(s) (they're recreated correctly by controller). Commands:
```
kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart daemonset/kube-proxy
kubectl delete endpointslice endpointslice-2 -n models
```
But check controller-manager and endpointslice-controller logs first — make sure it isn't repeatedly creating bad slices.

ajay.p: Doing that now. I'll restart kube-proxy on the three nodes showing the old conntrack entries. Also deleting the stale slice.

lucy.k: Follow-up: we should add a small preflight in our svc rollout job to check for endpointslice consistency after changing ports (wait for all slices to reflect new port) or add a short pause between svc update and traffic cutover. Filed a ticket to add that check.

keegan: Small cost/availability note — NLB health checks hit the stale node ports for ~2m which caused a fraction of requests to 503; not huge but visible in SLO graphs. Logging that as follow-up for runbook update.

deploy-bot: kube-proxy daemonset restarted on 3 nodes at 1799000350 — pods came back Ready.

ajay.p: After restart + slice delete, traffic normalized. Monitoring for 10m. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

devon.c: If this recurs, let's capture endpointslice-controller and kube-controller-manager metrics at the time of svc updates — probably a race between controller reconciliation and kube-proxy sync.

ajay.p: Will keep the rollout paused until we have the preflight in place. Closing if stable in 10m.

sre-bot: incidentbot: incident marked resolved at 1799000789 (duration ~11m)
